subject.title: Telegram: Auto-reply to unauthorized group senders with admin contact instructions

question: Should Telegram add an opt-in visible reply for group messages denied by `groupAllowFrom` or `groupPolicy`, and what default, cooldown, admin-contact, and raw-ID disclosure rules should it use?
rationale: This changes a fail-closed Telegram authorization boundary into visible group output, so automation cannot safely choose the product and privacy contract.

options.title: Add Opt-In Rate-Limited Notice
options.body: Add a default-off Telegram setting for denied-sender onboarding replies with per-sender cooldown, topic-aware delivery, and documented ID disclosure.

options.title: Route Through Operator Audit
options.body: Keep unauthorized senders silent and handle visibility through owner notification or audit work such as https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/77546.

options.title: Keep Silent Denial
options.body: Decline sender-facing replies for now and document logs, `/whoami`, and admin-driven ID collection as the supported secure posture.

recommendation.title: Add Opt-In Rate-Limited Notice
recommendation.body: Add a default-off Telegram setting for denied-sender onboarding replies with per-sender cooldown, topic-aware delivery, and documented ID disclosure.

likelyOwner.reason: Current blame and recent Telegram docs/config/channel history make this the strongest routing candidate for the product/security choice.
